description: Shenora: the hybrid app framework for .NET + React, portable across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS — reference it plus ONE shell package, or Shenora.Chromium for the kit's own Chromium shell, which is how it reaches macOS and Linux. Three layers: Core is the contract (the typed IPC stack with its middleware dispatcher and scoped router, the event bus, the webview interception and file-serving pipeline with the app's frontend served from a folder or embedded in its assembly, and the platform-neutral shell contracts — the IUiDispatcher UI-thread seam plus file dialogs, clipboard, URL launching, UI blocking, holding the window at an orientation, the app's colour scheme, a window's system animations and a native launcher's startup screen, so application logic compiles with no Windows reference — and what both desktop shells share: the single-instance guard that hands a later launch's arguments to the running app, window-state persistence, revealing files and launching processes, naming who holds a file open, and the unhandled-exception report). Core also holds the auxiliary browser sessions, written once over the browsers each shell makes: a bounded pool of off-screen sessions, an interactive session over an isolated persistent profile, and streaming sessions (screencast out, synthetic input in); mechanisms only, the kit ships no workflow. Engine is the brain (the mission scheduler with claims, lanes and durable queues; journalled safe file mutation with path locks). Modules bridge .NET to the web (media probing, planning, remuxing, streamed range delivery and platform codec conversion, plus the shell's own PICTURE SURFACE — on a phone a film the webview refuses is drawn by the platform's player under a transparent region the page leaves, with no transcode and the page keeping every control; native file dialogs; Live Activities and playback sessions; request tracking; staged self-update with safe archive extraction; versioned resource packs whose boot decision cannot skip the packaged-vs-fetched version comparison; the system back gesture offered to the page per press, foreground transitions carrying how long the app was away, and holding the window portrait or landscape — which a page cannot do for itself, since its own screen.orientation.lock() works only in fullscreen). The outbound notification path reports what it accepted, filtered, dropped and delivered, so "my page receives no events" is answerable without guessing. Application host and builder via ShenoraApplication.CreateBuilder. Depends on Microsoft.Extensions DI (implementation) + logging abstractions.
